Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Fairview Public Library. I'm Megan, and I look after new memberships here.
We're open Monday to Saturday, from nine until eight in the evening, but closed on Sundays.
Membership itself is completely free for local residents, so there's no charge to sign up today.
You're allowed to borrow up to eight items at a time, which includes books, DVDs, and magazines.
The standard loan period is three weeks, though you can renew online if you need longer.
If something's returned late, there's a small fine of twenty cents per day.

Now, let me tell you a bit more about what we offer beyond just borrowing books.

Our children's section has its own dedicated reading corner, and we run a story time every Saturday morning that's always fully booked within a day of opening — so it's worth signing up the moment slots appear online, rather than waiting.
lines.note: Paper: A Story time has no time limit; B Story time slots fill up quickly; C Story time is for adults only.

lines.text: If you need a quiet space to work, our study room upstairs is fairly small, so during exam season especially, we'd really recommend reserving a desk in advance rather than just turning up and hoping.
lines.note: Paper: A The study room is always empty; B The study room cannot be booked; C Booking ahead is strongly advised.

lines.text: We also have a small computer lab, and while walk-ins are welcome, we do prioritise anyone doing job applications or official paperwork if things get busy.
lines.note: Paper: A Job-seekers get priority when busy; B Only members can use the computers; C The lab is for children only.

lines.text: As for our meeting room, it's free to book for community groups, though we do ask that any commercial use be arranged separately with the main office.
lines.note: Paper: A The meeting room is never free; B Commercial bookings need separate arrangement; C Only staff can use the meeting room.

lines.text: And finally, if you ever have trouble finding something, don't hesitate to ask — most of us have been here for years and genuinely enjoy tracking down obscure requests.
lines.note: Paper: A Staff prefer not to be disturbed; B Only the front desk can help; C Staff are happy to help with any request.

lines.text: That's everything for today — welcome again, and enjoy the library.
That is the end of Section Two. Now turn to Section Three.
